title: Benchmark begins public consultation on updating quality specifications and representative producers for its cobalt hydroxide CIF Asia price assessment
gist: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence opened a public consultation, with feedback due 27 November 2026, on tightening quality specifications for its CIF Asia cobalt hydroxide price assessment, including raising minimum cobalt content from 20% to 30%, and on naming representative producers.

insights.claim: Benchmark proposes lifting the minimum cobalt content for its CIF Asia cobalt hydroxide assessment to 30%, from a current methodology that specifies a typical 20-40%, and the assessed grade would change from Min 20% to Min 30%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The reference price will track higher-grade material, so the published series may shift or break versus history.
insights.quote: Cobalt Hydroxide; Min 30%; CIF Asia; USD/Tonne

insights.claim: Proposed maximum impurity limits are Mn 6.5%, Mg 6.5%, Cu 2.5% and Fe 1%, compared with current thresholds of Cu below 10%, Fe below 2%, Mn below 5% and Mg below 10%.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Copper and magnesium limits tighten sharply while manganese is loosened, so some previously acceptable feed would fall outside the assessment.
insights.quote: Benchmark proposes to define the assessment on the basis of cobalt content of 30% minimum

insights.claim: New maximum limits are proposed for S at 5%, Zn at 1%, Ca at 1.5%, Ni at 1.5%, Al at 0.2% and Cd at 100 ppm, plus a requirement regarding natural radioactivity.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Radioactivity and cadmium limits reflect refinery acceptability and compliance concerns in the physical market.

insights.claim: Benchmark says certain quality parameters can materially affect the acceptability and value of cobalt hydroxide, and the tighter spec aims to reflect material considered mainstream in the physical market.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Price discovery is being aligned with what refiners will actually buy, implying a discount for off-spec material.
insights.quote: certain quality parameters can materially affect the acceptability and value of cobalt hydroxide

insights.claim: Benchmark proposes naming KFM, TFM, KCC, Mumi, ERG Metakol, Deziwa, Kimin and Somika as representative brands and producers for the assessment.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The list maps the DRC-centred hydroxide supply that sets the reference price; producers outside it may be priced at discounts.
insights.quote: These would include KFM, TFM, KCC, Mumi, ERG Metakol, Deziwa, Kimin and Somika.

insights.claim: Benchmark invites feedback from active market participants by 27 November 2026 via prices@benchmarkminerals.com, after discussion with market participants prompted the proposal.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: The methodology change would take effect after the consultation, so watch for the effective date and any back-series treatment.
insights.quote: Benchmark invites feedback from active market participants by the latest 27th November 2026.
